## The idea

Many choices pay off only if the people around us make the same one: which side of the road to drive on, which messaging app to use, which greeting to offer, which word to use for a fizzy drink. The local majority model places people on a grid and lets each one switch to whatever most of their eight neighbours do. It is the behaviour of a player in a *pure coordination game* against each neighbour, choosing the action that matches the majority (a myopic best response).

Locally, the rule works: everyone ends up agreeing with most of their neighbours, and the grid freezes. Globally, it need not produce agreement at all. Unless one action starts with a clear majority, the grid freezes into a patchwork of regions, each internally coordinated and different from its neighbours. Page calls this the *paradox of coordination*: local coordination produces global diversity, which is one explanation for regional dialects, customs and standards.

## Formulation

::: {.model-box}
**Setup.** Each cell of a two-dimensional grid (here $60 \times 60$, wrapped at the edges) is in one of two states, on or off. Each cell has eight neighbours.

**Rule.** In each period a cell is chosen at random. It changes state if and only if five or more of its eight neighbours are in the other state.

**Results.** The process always stops: eventually no cell wants to change (an equilibrium). In that equilibrium every cell agrees with at least four of its neighbours, but unless one state starts with a clear majority, both states survive in patches. *Paradox of coordination:* if people coordinate locally, global configurations will be patchy and diverse.
:::

Each cell is a player in a pure coordination game with each neighbour (payoff 1 for matching, 0 otherwise); switching to the majority of the neighbourhood maximizes its payoff given the neighbours' current actions. That the process must stop is shown on the [Lyapunov functions](lyapunov-functions.qmd) page: every switch strictly increases the number of matching neighbour pairs.

## Interactive model

One run, replayed in your browser: teal cells are on, orange cells off. Step through the sweeps (each sweep is as many single-cell updates as there are cells) or press **Play**. The grid freezes within a few dozen sweeps into a patchwork. Move the initial share away from 50% and the majority takes over.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
import {rng, torus8, drawGrid, player, C, pct} from "../js/models.js"
```

```{ojs}
viewof shareOn = Inputs.range([10, 90], {value: 50, step: 5, label: "Initial share on (%)"})
viewof seed = Inputs.range([1, 500], {value: 30, step: 1, label: "Random seed"})
```

```{ojs}
majority = {
  const r = rng(seed), n = 60, N = n * n, nb = torus8(n);
  const on = new Uint8Array(N);
  for (let i = 0; i < N; i++) on[i] = r() * 100 < shareOn ? 1 : 0;
  const differ = i => { let d = 0; for (let k = 0; k < 8; k++) if (on[nb[8 * i + k]] !== on[i]) d++; return d; };
  const anyUnstable = () => { for (let i = 0; i < N; i++) if (differ(i) >= 5) return true; return false; };
  const stats = () => {
    let s = 0, b = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < N; i++) { s += on[i]; if (differ(i) > 0) b++; }
    return {on: s / N, boundary: b / N};
  };
  const frames = [on.slice()], series = [{sweep: 0, ...stats()}];
  for (let sweep = 1; sweep <= 100 && anyUnstable(); sweep++) {
    for (let k = 0; k < N; k++) { const i = Math.floor(r() * N); if (differ(i) >= 5) on[i] = 1 - on[i]; }
    frames.push(on.slice());
    series.push({sweep, ...stats()});
  }
  return {n, frames, series, frozen: !anyUnstable()};
}
```

```{ojs}
viewof sweep = player(majority.frames.length - 1, {label: "Sweep", delay: 200})
```

```{ojs}
drawGrid(majority.frames[sweep], majority.n, [C.orange, C.teal], {
  size: 420,
  ariaLabel: "Local Majority Model: the grid",
  ariaDescription: "A 60 by 60 grid; teal cells are on and orange cells are off. The summary below the charts states the result in words."
})
```

```{ojs}
Plot.plot({
  ariaLabel: "Local Majority Model: share on and boundary cells over time",
  ariaDescription: "Horizontal axis: sweep. Vertical axis: share of cells. The teal line is the share of cells that are on; the purple line is the share of cells with at least one neighbour in the other state. The summary below the charts states the result in words.",
  height: 200,
  x: {label: "Sweep"},
  y: {label: "Share of cells", domain: [0, 1], tickFormat: "%", grid: true},
  color: {legend: true, domain: ["Cells on", "Cells on a boundary"], range: [C.teal, C.purple]},
  marks: [
    Plot.line(majority.series, {x: "sweep", y: "on", stroke: () => "Cells on", strokeWidth: 2}),
    Plot.line(majority.series, {x: "sweep", y: "boundary", stroke: () => "Cells on a boundary", strokeWidth: 2}),
    Plot.ruleX([sweep], {stroke: "currentColor", strokeOpacity: 0.4})
  ]
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const first = majority.series[0], last = majority.series[majority.series.length - 1];
  return html`<div class="sim-readout">${md`The grid started with ${pct(first.on)} of cells on and ${pct(first.boundary)} of cells next to a disagreeing neighbour. ${majority.frozen ? `It **froze after ${last.sweep} sweeps**` : `After ${last.sweep} sweeps it was still changing`}, with **${pct(last.on)}** of cells on and **${pct(last.boundary)}** still on a boundary between regions. ${last.on > 0.02 && last.on < 0.98 ? "Everyone agrees with most of their neighbours, yet both states survive: local coordination, global diversity." : "One state took over the whole grid."}`}</div>`;
}
```

### NetLogo experiment

The same model in NetLogo (a 60 × 60 wrapped grid), run by nlrx at nine initial shares with six seeds each, until the grid froze. Dots are individual runs; the dashed diagonal marks a final share equal to the initial one.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
nlRuns = FileAttachment("../data/local-majority.csv").csv({typed: true})
nlMeans = d3.rollups(nlRuns, v => ({final: d3.mean(v, d => d.final_on), boundary: d3.mean(v, d => d.boundary_share), sweeps: d3.mean(v, d => d.step)}), d => d.share_on).map(([s, m]) => ({share: s / 100, ...m})).sort((a, b) => a.share - b.share)
```

```{ojs}
Plot.plot({
  ariaLabel: "Local Majority Model: NetLogo experiment",
  ariaDescription: "Horizontal axis: initial share of cells on. Vertical axis: share on when the grid froze (teal dots and line) and share of cells on a boundary (purple line). The dashed diagonal marks no change. The summary below the chart states the result in words.",
  height: 300,
  x: {label: "Initial share on", domain: [0, 1], tickFormat: "%"},
  y: {label: "Share of cells when frozen", domain: [0, 1], tickFormat: "%", grid: true},
  color: {legend: true, domain: ["Cells on", "Cells on a boundary"], range: [C.teal, C.purple]},
  marks: [
    Plot.line([[0, 0], [1, 1]], {stroke: "currentColor", strokeDasharray: "4 3", strokeOpacity: 0.6}),
    Plot.dot(nlRuns, {x: d => d.share_on / 100, y: "final_on", fill: C.teal, r: 3, fillOpacity: 0.6}),
    Plot.line(nlMeans, {x: "share", y: "final", stroke: () => "Cells on", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
    Plot.line(nlMeans, {x: "share", y: "boundary", stroke: () => "Cells on a boundary", strokeWidth: 2.5, marker: "circle"})
  ]
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const at = s => nlMeans.find(d => Math.abs(d.share - s) < 1e-9);
  const a40 = at(0.4), a50 = at(0.5), a60 = at(0.6);
  return html`<div class="sim-readout">${md`In NetLogo, local conformity **amplifies the initial majority**: grids starting 40% on froze at ${pct(a40.final)} on, and grids starting 60% on froze at ${pct(a60.final)}. From an even start, grids froze at ${pct(a50.final)} on average with **${pct(a50.boundary)} of cells on a boundary**: a patchwork, the paradox of coordination. The slowest setting took ${Math.round(d3.max(nlMeans, d => d.sweeps))} sweeps on average to freeze.`}</div>`;
}
```

## NetLogo {.unlisted}

```{.netlogo}
; The local majority model (The Model Thinker, chapter 15).
; The Model Thinker Companion: reference implementation, run with nlrx by
; abm/local-majority.R. The page replays the same rules in JavaScript.
;
; Each cell of a wrapped grid is on or off. One tick is one sweep: as many
; single-cell updates as there are cells. In each update a random cell is
; chosen and it switches state if and only if five or more of its eight
; neighbours are in the other state. The run stops when no cell would switch.

globals [
  initial-on      ; share of cells on at the start
]

patches-own [ on? ]

to setup
  clear-all
  ask patches [
    set on? random-float 100 < share-on
    recolor
  ]
  set initial-on final-on
  reset-ticks
end

to go
  if not any? patches with [ unstable? ] [ stop ]
  repeat count patches [
    ask one-of patches [
      if unstable? [ set on? not on? recolor ]
    ]
  ]
  tick
end

to-report unstable?
  report count neighbors with [ on? != [ on? ] of myself ] >= 5
end

to recolor
  set pcolor ifelse-value on? [ 85 ] [ 26 ]
end

; Share of cells on.
to-report final-on
  report count patches with [ on? ] / count patches
end

; Share of cells with at least one neighbour in the other state: a measure
; of how patchy the configuration is (0 means one uniform block).
to-report boundary-share
  report count patches with [ any? neighbors with [ on? != [ on? ] of myself ] ]
    / count patches
end
```

## nlrx (R) {.unlisted}

```{.r}
# The local majority model: how does the initial mix shape the frozen
# configuration? Does the majority take over, and how patchy is the result?
# NetLogo model: abm/local-majority.nlogo. Output: data/local-majority.csv
# (one row per initial share and seed).
source("abm/_nlrx.R")

nl <- nl_model("local-majority")
nl@experiment <- experiment(
  expname = "share_sweep",
  outpath = tempdir(),
  repetition = 1,
  tickmetrics = "false", # measure once, when the grid has frozen
  idsetup = "setup",
  idgo = "go",
  runtime = 100, # cap; runs stop when no cell would switch
  metrics = c("initial-on", "final-on", "boundary-share"),
  variables = list(
    "share-on" = list(values = c(20, 30, 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, 70, 80))
  ),
  constants = list()
)
set.seed(15) # makes nlrx draw the same NetLogo seeds every time
nl@simdesign <- simdesign_ff(nl, nseeds = 6)

results <- run_experiment(nl)
save_results(results, "local-majority",
  keep = c(
    "share_on", "random_seed", "step", "initial_on", "final_on",
    "boundary_share"
  )
)
```

## Takeaways

::: takeaways
- Conforming to the local majority always settles into an equilibrium.
- Local coordination does not imply global coordination: the equilibrium is usually a patchwork of regions.
- A clear initial majority is amplified and takes over; a close split freezes into lasting diversity.
:::

## Uses

::: uses
- **Explain.** Regional dialects (*pop* versus *soda*), customs, technology standards and political cultures that persist side by side.
- **Reason.** Why convergence on a single standard often needs a global push (a law, a dominant firm) rather than local imitation.
- **Explore.** Vary the neighbourhood, the threshold or the update order and see when patches survive.
:::

## Related models

- [Schelling's Segregation Model](schelling-segregation.qmd): agents move rather than switch, with a similar patchwork result.
- [Game of Life](game-of-life.qmd): another local rule on the same grid, with very different dynamics.
- [Lyapunov Functions](lyapunov-functions.qmd): the argument that the process must stop.
- [Polya Process](polya-process.qmd): another route by which early randomness becomes lasting structure.
